summary: Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and 1993, and held a post at the University of Washington around 1995.

Ana Agud is a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Salamanca (~1965–1970) and the University of Tübingen (~1970–1974). From around 1980 to 2018, she served as a professor at the University of Salamanca.

Anagarika Dharmapala (1864–1933) was an active figure in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya, St. Benedict's College, S. Thomas' College, and Royal College, and founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891.

Anagarika Govinda (1898–1985) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied in Italy and Germany, taught at Visva-Bharati and Patna universities, and founded and led the Arya Maitreya Mandala (~1933–1985).

Anagarika Munindra (1915–2003) was active in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as superintendent of the Mahabodhi Temple (1953–1957) and studied under Satya Narayan Goenka and Mahasi Sayadaw (1957–1966).
Anam Thubten Rinpoche works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Tsurlo Rinpoche and held a post as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation College of Buddhist Studies.

Ananda Guruge (1928–2014) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. After earning degrees from the University of Ceylon and the University of London, he taught at NIEPA (attested 1970), California State University, Fullerton, and University of the West (attested 2012).

Ananda Kentish Coomaraswamy (1877–1947) was a scholar in Indology, history and archaeology, and religious studies. Educated at University College London, he directed the Geological Survey of Ceylon (~1903–1906) and was a curator and fellow at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.

Anant Sadashiv Altekar (1898–1959) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (~1930–1949) and Patna University (~1949–1957), and directed the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1950–1959).

Anantalal Thakur (1916–2009) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Calcutta under various teachers and held posts as professor at the Mithila Institute (~1955–1969) and director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (1968–1971).

Anantanand Rambachan is a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of the West Indies, under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, and at the University of Leeds, serving as a professor of religion at St. Olaf College (~1985–2021).

Andrea Acri is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Leiden University under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, worked there as a junior researcher (~2006–2010), and joined the École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2016.
Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned her PhD from Rice University in 2010. She joined Indiana University in 2010, eventually becoming a full professor in 2021.
Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed both her Magister degree (by 2008) and her PhD (by 2014) at the Free University of Berlin.

Andreas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura and trained under traditional teachers including Chökyi Nyima Rinpoche and Tsikey Chokling Rinpoche.
Andreas Spengel (1838–1905) was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his studies at the University of Munich (~1856–1860) and the University of Berlin (~1860–1862).

Andree Dominique Messent is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Messent earned a PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams and also studied under Rupert Gethin and Ulrich Pagel.
Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov (1904–1937) was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky).
Andrew B. Irvine works in philosophy and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Boston University and held a post as assistant professor of philosophy at Maryville College (attested 2009).
Andrew Garrett is a linguist who completed his studies at Harvard University (~1983–1990). He has held a post at the University of California, Berkeley since around 1995.
